problem: Existing token caching methods for VLA/VLM models select cacheable tokens with visual-domain (position-wise similarity) criteria, which fail under viewpoint migration, cannot perceive critical obstacle edges without extra models, and use static cache budgets that ignore temporal scene-complexity changes.
motivation: VLN models must run expensive inference every step, which blocks real-time deployment. Consecutive frames are highly redundant, so training-free token caching is attractive, but visual-domain selection either misses reusable shifted tokens or wrongly reuses edge tokens (causing collisions). The frequency domain offers translation-invariant amplitude, separable high-frequency edge energy, and spectral entropy as a complexity proxy.
key_idea: Use frequency-domain properties (amplitude-spectrum shift invariance with phase correlation, high-frequency DCT energy for edges, spectral entropy for budget) to decide which visual tokens to reuse across VLN timesteps.
insight: Each frequency-domain cue targets one failure mode of visual-domain caching. Ablations show removing edge-aware refresh (Module II) costs the most accuracy (SR -4.2, SPL -4.4), removing migration alignment (Module I) cuts token reuse from 53.5% to 19.8% (speedup 1.05x), and replacing the entropy-adaptive budget with a fixed 30% ratio reduces speedup to 1.52x. A naive position-wise FFT amplitude baseline performs poorly (SR 53.4, 1.08x), so gains come from the specific alignment, edge and budget design, not from using the frequency domain alone.
method: Migration-Aware Cache Establishment (Module I): 2D FFT amplitude cosine similarity between consecutive feature maps; if below tau_mig=0.12 the cache is flushed, otherwise phase correlation (cross-power spectrum, inverse FFT peak) estimates displacement (di,dj) and builds an alignment mask; unaligned new-view patches are recomputed.

Edge-Related Token Identification (Module II): block-wise 2D DCT per patch, high-pass mask removing the low-frequency quadrant (P/4), patch high-frequency energy E; patches with E > mu_E + lambda*sigma_E (lambda=0.25) are force-refreshed.

Temporal Adaptive Budget (Module III): spectral entropy of the normalized amplitude spectrum is mapped by alpha_t = alpha_min + (alpha_max-alpha_min)e^{-Psi} (alpha_max=0.5, alpha_min=0.08); K_reuse = floor(alpha_t*N).
Fusion and token selection: candidates are tokens with Mask_align=1 and Mask_fresh=0; sorted by ascending high-frequency energy and the top K_reuse are reused, K_final = min(K_reuse, K_candidate).

System implementation: ~5000 lines PyTorch/CUDA; three GPU processes (VLN inference on tensor cores, cuFFT frequency modules run in parallel, SIMT token selection kernels) synchronized before fusion, with under 2.54 ms overhead per step.

setting.backbone: InternVLA-N1 (7B, built on Qwen2.5-VL), frozen, with FreqCache as a training-free plug-in
setting.observation: egocentric monocular RGB frames (consecutive-frame visual features)
setting.action_space: continuous-environment VLN-CE actions predicted by InternVLA-N1 (low-level)

numbers.extra: Training-free token caching; the paper says only 'R2R-CE' and does not name the split, so val-unseen is assumed. Uncached baseline: NE 4.05, OS 70.7, SR 64.3, SPL 58.5. Speedup 1.59x, latency 401 ms/step vs 637 ms, token reuse 53.5%.
numbers.evidence: Table 1 'Navigation Accuracy Comparison on R2R-CE' and Table 2 'Inference Efficiency Comparison on R2R-CE'

numbers_note: The split is not stated in the paper; val-unseen is assumed. Table 1 gives OS, mapped here to OSR.
results: On InternVLA-N1 in R2R-CE, FreqCache gives a 1.59x step and episode speedup (637 to 401 ms/step) with 53.5% token reuse, and SR 63.0 / SPL 57.2 against 64.3 / 58.5 uncached. It beats the VLN-Cache variants (up to 1.55x with 36% reuse, SR 54.6-63.1) and the naive frequency baseline (1.08x, SR 53.4).
limitations: Evaluated only on one backbone (InternVLA-N1) and one benchmark (R2R-CE) in simulation; no real-robot tests.
Slight accuracy drop versus no caching (SR 64.3 to 63.0); hyperparameters (tau_mig, lambda, alpha bounds) are set empirically.
Phase correlation assumes a global translation between frames, which only roughly models rotation and perspective distortion.
